newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm on low U.S. product stocks.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm on low U.S. product stocks.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures drifted off session highs in late trade but still closed firm, underpinned by U.S. products inventory data, dealers said.
Oct Brent closed up 25 cents at $20.28 a barrel after touching a midafternoon high of $20.51 as U.S. products markets surged on falling gasoline stocks.
"There's been a bit of profit-taking but overall low U.S. stocks were the key factor again," said a broker.
The Energy Information Agency (EIA) said U.S. gasoline stocks fell 2.1 million barrels in the week to August 23, confirming earlier American Petroleum Institute (API) figures.

Bullish U.S. products -- NYMEX gasoline put on nearly two percent or over a cent a gallon -- overcame initial bearish sentiment sparked by a 10-million barrel build in U.S. crude stocks, which some traders attributed to reporting delays.

Earlier, IPE gas oil closed at a new four-month high amid concern about low heating oil inventories in the U.S. as the winter approaches. Sept gas oil finished $2.50 higher at $191.75 a tonne, the highest front-month price since April 11.
U.S. distillate stocks rose 700,000 barrels but were still lagging well behind year-ago levels, the EIA data showed.
